'''Janice''' is the lead guitar player in [[Dr. Teeth and the Electric Mayhem|The Electric Mayhem]] on ''[[The Muppet Show]]''. She also portrays Nurse Janice in [[Veterinarian's Hospital]], and appears in various other sketches, frequently as a chorus member. She is occasionally seen in the [[The Muppet Orchestra|orchestra]] during the fifth season of the show. She has a very close relationship with the Electric Mayhem's bass player, [[Floyd Pepper]] (although, in the first season of ''The Muppet Show'', she's involved with [[Zoot]] in the ''At the Dance ''sketch).

In addition to the guitar, Janice has also played the tambourine with the Mayhem, and the trumpet or trombone with the orchestra. In personality, Janice is generally laid-back, noted for her Valley girl "Fer sure" and "Rully" dialogue and behavior (such as tanning herself in ''[[The Great Muppet Caper]]''). Twice in the Muppet movies, when caught short during a loud and confusing group discussion, Janice has inadvertently revealed her attitudes towards [[Naked Muppets|nudity]]. In ''The Great Muppet Caper'', she's interrupted while justifying a willingness to walk along the beach naked to her mother, while in ''[[The Muppets Take Manhattan]]'', she claims that she doesn't pose naked, "even if it is artistic." Janice also has an affinity for baking, at least during the holidays: in ''[[A Muppet Family Christmas]]'', she makes Christmas cookies that are eaten by [[Cookie Monster]], while she brings cupcakes to the party in ''[[A Muppets Christmas: Letters to Santa]]''. She lists [[Tina Turner]] and [[Joan Jett]] among her musical influences, and [[Weezer]] and [[OK Go]] as some of her favorite current bands.<ref>[http://www.whatsthatdudeplay.com/2011/11/wtdp-exclusive-mayhem-returns-2/ WTDP? Exclusive: Mayhem Returns! Veterans Dr. Teeth & The Electric Mayhem keep on rockin’. November 7, 2011. whatsthatdudeplay.com.]</ref>

Janice was originally performed by [[Fran Brill]] in ''[[The Muppet Show: Sex and Violence]]'' pilot in 1975, and in the first set of ''[[Muppet Meeting Films]]''. [[Eren Ozker]] performed Janice in the first season of ''The Muppet Show''. [[Richard Hunt]] took over the character in season two, and gave Janice her familiar Valley girl voice and attitude.

[[Michael K. Frith|Michael Frith]]'s original sketch of the character indicates that she was intended to be a male character, a takeoff on [[Mick Jagger]]'s emaciated frame and prominent lips. Her name is probably a reference to Janis Joplin. However, in her final form as built by [[Bonnie Erickson]], she bears very little resemblance to either Jagger or Joplin.

In an August 27, 2015 [[Twitter|tweet]], @ElectricMayhem revealed a never before known fact about Janice's family, "Janice truly is a flower child. Her mom's name was Daisy!" [https://twitter.com/ElectricMayhem/status/637012511657697280]

''[[The Muppets Mayhem]]'' revealed that Janice is allergic to all forms of lying, which causes her to sneeze.  After [[Nora Singh]] lies so much Janice becomes deathly ill until she told the truth to her and the band. [[Track 4: The Times They Are A-Changin'|Episode four]] revealed that Janice has a [[Twins|twin]] sister whom she has had a falling out with, but never goes into detail why.  This event makes Janice form a habit of putting other people's problems and needs before her own.  After a hallucinogenic episode involving a pack of expired marshmallows, she realized that she needs to start thinking more about herself.

'''Meryl Sheep''' appeared on ''[[Sesame Street]]'' as a spoof of the actress [[Meryl Streep]]. She was introduced in [[Season 18 (1986-1987)|season 18]] in [[1987]], following the success of another parody Muppet, [[Placido Flamingo]]. [[Norman Stiles]] described her as "a sheep, with a middle European accent, somewhat reminiscent of someone we knew in ''[[Sophie's Choice]]'', but not exactly."<ref>''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''. November 9, 1987.</ref> During her stint on the series, Meryl Sheep taught many students at the Meryl Sheep School of Acting, including [[Susan Sarandon]]. The character made recurring appearances through [[Season 21 (1989-1990)|season 21]].

On November 14, 1988, Meryl Sheep co-hosted ''[[Today|The Today Show]]'' with [[Count von Count]]. Bonora performed the character at [[Jim Henson's Memorial]]. She was also seen as a part of a distinguished panel of American Muppets in ''[[Free to Be... a Family (special)|Free to Be... a Family]]''.

Meryl was the subject of several press interviews prior to her expanded role on the show in [[Season 19 (1987-1988)|Season 19]]. In a profile for ''[[People]]'', she claims to have grown up on a small farm and was brought into show business by Sam the Sepherd.<ref>'' People'' "NEVER FLUFFING HER LINES, SESAME STREET'S MERYL SHEEP IS TV'S NEW DYED-IN-THE-WOOL STAR"  1/25/88, Vol. 29, Issue 3</ref> In another interview, Meryl states that she lives in an apartment above a theater on Sesame Street, and remarks that she has no qualms with there being another Meryl in show business (but believes she came first).<ref>''Newsday Suffolk Edition'' "The Real Meryl Sheep Speaks Up" November 29, 1987</ref>

Meryl was initially recycled from a stock lamb puppet used on the show as early as [[Sesame Street News Flash: Don Music: Old MacDonald|1976]], but with more feminine eyes and an added wig (which would alternate between blonde and brunette). Starting in [[Season 20 (1988-1989)|season 20]], a new version of the puppet was introduced: her face was completely redone and dyed to match her wool, and she retained a permanently brunette hairdo. This puppet would go on to become a utility puppet by [[Season 22 (1990-1991)|season 22]], and was also used as [[Baabra Sheep]] on ''[[Panwapa]]''.  The puppet was also modified and used as a goat in the ''[[Elmo the Musical]]'' segment "[[Elmo the Musical: Mountain Climber the Musical|Mountain Climber the Musical]]", as well as [[Episode 112: Olivia Wilde / Sara Bareilles|episode 12]] of ''[[The Not-Too-Late Show with Elmo]]''.

Several years after she was dropped as a recurring character, [[Prairie Dawn]] is seen reading a book by Meryl entitled "10 Days to a New Ewe" in [[Episode 3832]].
